transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my appetite has been really inconsistent for months. Some days I just skip dinner and I’ve lost some weight without trying, and other nights I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal because making a real meal for myself feels kind of pointless.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I wouldn’t say I’m crying all the time or anything. I’ve just felt kind of flat, I guess, and not myself.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah… I think so. I still do things I used to enjoy, like watering my garden or going to book club, but it just feels kind of flat now. A lot of the time I either leave early or I don’t even get myself to start.
Have you lost a significant amount of weight over these months?

Yes, I have lost some weight without trying. I don’t know if I’d call it a huge amount, but it’s noticeable to me. My appetite’s been pretty up and down for months—some nights I skip dinner, and other nights I just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking feels pointless.
Have you had any episodes where you ate a large amount of food in a short period of time?

No, not really large amounts. It’s more the opposite or just kind of inconsistent—some nights I skip dinner, and other nights I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking feels pointless. My appetite’s just been all over the place.
Do you often feel guilty or criticize yourself for things that have happened?

Yes. I do that a lot. I keep replaying my marriage in my head and thinking I must have failed at something pretty basic. I know, rationally, relationships are more complicated than that, but I still end up blaming myself.
Have you ever eaten until you felt uncomfortably full?

No, not really. I haven’t been eating to the point of feeling uncomfortably full. It’s been more that my appetite is unpredictable — sometimes I skip dinner, and other nights I just pick at something small like crackers or cereal because making a meal feels pointless.
Have you ever had an episode where you felt like you couldn't stop eating once you started?
I don’t think so. I haven’t had times where I felt out of control with eating or like I couldn’t stop once I started.
Do you feel sad most of the time?
I’m not sure I’d say most of the time. I do feel sad pretty often, but it comes and goes. Some days are just heavier than others.
Would you say the weight you've lost is more than 5% of your original body weight?

I’m not sure if it’s more than 5%. I have lost some weight without trying, though. My appetite has been really uneven for months — sometimes I skip dinner, and other nights I just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking feels pointless.
Has your weight loss been more than 5% of your body weight since this all started?

I honestly don’t know the exact percentage. I have lost weight without trying, though. My appetite’s been all over the place for months — some evenings I just skip dinner, and other nights I’ll just have crackers or cereal because cooking for myself feels pointless.
Has a doctor or healthcare provider told you that you have lost a significant amount of weight?

No, not specifically. No one’s told me it was a significant amount. I’ve just noticed I’ve lost some weight without trying, mostly because my appetite’s been so off and I’ll skip dinner or just eat crackers or cereal instead of making something.
Has your weight loss been noticeable to others, such as friends or family members?

I don’t think anyone’s really commented on it directly. I’ve noticed it myself, though — my appetite has been so inconsistent for months, and I’ll go through stretches where I skip dinner or just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking feels pointless. So I have lost some weight without trying.
Has your weight loss had any impact on your physical health?

Mostly just that I don’t feel like I’m taking care of myself very well. I’ve lost some weight without trying because my appetite’s been so up and down, and there are stretches where I skip dinner or just eat crackers or cereal. I wouldn’t say I know of a specific health problem from it, but it’s part of what made me realize I should come in.
Has your weight loss been significant enough that you've had to buy smaller clothes or adjust your belt to a tighter notch?

Not really to the point of buying smaller clothes or anything like that. I’ve noticed I’ve lost some weight without trying, mainly because my appetite’s been all over the place for months. Some nights I skip dinner, or I’ll just have crackers or cereal because cooking for myself feels pointless.
Have you had to make any changes to your daily routine because of your weight loss?

Not really because of the weight loss itself, no. It’s more that my routine around eating has gotten pretty off. Some evenings I just skip dinner, or I’ll have crackers or cereal instead of cooking because it feels pointless. That’s been going on for months, and I’ve lost weight without trying.
Do you usually eat less when you're feeling sad or flat?

Yes, I think so. When I’m feeling sad or kind of flat, eating just feels like too much effort. I’ll skip dinner, or I’ll just pick at crackers or cereal instead of cooking. That’s been happening on and off for months, and I’ve lost some weight without meaning to.
Do you think your inconsistent appetite is directly related to how you're feeling emotionally?

Yes, I think it is. When I’m feeling low, cooking for myself just feels pointless, so I’ll skip dinner or just pick at crackers or cereal. It’s been like that for months, and I’ve lost some weight without trying.
Has a healthcare provider expressed concern about your weight loss?

Not really from a provider yet. What finally made me come in is that my appetite has been so inconsistent for months—some nights I skip dinner, other nights I just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking feels pointless—and I’ve been losing weight without trying.
Has your weight loss been significant enough that a healthcare provider has recommended you see a specialist or get further evaluation for it?

No, no one’s referred me to a specialist or anything like that. It’s more that my appetite has been all over the place for months, and I’ll go through stretches where I skip dinner or just pick at crackers or cereal because cooking feels pointless. I’ve lost some weight without trying, and that’s part of what finally made me come in.
